videos.title: NEW Porsche Cayenne Turbo v Ferrari 296 DRAG RACE
videos.summary_source_text:
NEW Porsche Cayenne Turbo v Ferrari 296 DRAG RACE It’s time for an electric vs exotic drag race showdown!

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-120926

We’ve pitted an ultra-high-tech plug-in hybrid supercar against a heavy-hitting, twin-motor family hauler to see if instant EV torque can outrun pure Italian pedigree! It’s the Ferrari 296 taking on the all-new Porsche Cayenne EV!

Can thousands of pounds of luxury SUV really hold off Maranello's finest off the line? Let’s check out the stats…

Starting with the Ferrari 296, it’s powered by a 3.0-litre twin-turbo V6 mid-engined hybrid setup, pumping out a staggering 830hp and 740Nm of torque. All that power is sent strictly to the rear wheels via an 8-speed automatic gearbox, and thanks to built-in launch control, it squeezes every bit of performance out of its sleek 1,640kg body. It’s an absolute engineering masterpiece, but perfection doesn't come cheap, this beauty will set you back £279,343!

Then we come to the challenger: the all-electric Porsche Cayenne EV. Don't let the SUV shape fool you; this monster packs two electric motors delivering an astonishing 1,156hp and a back-breaking 1,500Nm of instant torque! It's an absolute titan on the scales at 2,645kg, but with all-wheel drive traction launching all that instant power, it moves like a guided missile. The price tag? A surprisingly accessible £130,900 alongside the Ferrari!

So, the Cayenne EV has a massive 326hp advantage and double the torque of the Ferrari, but can it overcome a massive 1-tonne weight penalty when the lights go out? There’s only one way to find out for sure… LET’S RACE!

videos.summary_source_text:
Ready in 3 minutes! A healthy, protein-rich chia dessert. Sugar-free! Lactose-free! Ready in 3 minutes! A healthy chocolate dessert made with chia seeds, flax seeds, and cocoa agar—sugar-free, lactose-free, gelatin-free, and high in protein. It's the perfect healthy dessert for those on a healthy, vegan, lactose-free, or gluten-free diet, as well as for anyone trying to lose weight but still enjoying a sweet tooth.

Why this dessert is so healthy:
- Chia seeds are a superfood rich in plant-based protein, omega-3, fiber, and calcium
- White flax seeds are a source of omega-3, lignans, and fiber, beneficial for digestion and hormonal balance
- Agar-agar is a plant-based gelatin substitute made from algae, calorie-free, and vegan-friendly
- Cocoa contains natural antioxidants, magnesium, and a true chocolate flavor without sugar

What you'll find in this video:
- A quick recipe for a chocolate chia and flax dessert in just 3 minutes
- A healthy alternative to candy and chocolate without sugar or milk
- Agar-based dessert that holds its shape like panna cotta or chocolate pudding
- Suitable for breakfast, snacks, kids' menus, and weekly meal prep

1/2 cup (125 ml) coconut milk. 1/4 cup (20 g) cocoa powder.
2 tsp agar-agar.
1/4 cup (60 ml) water.
3.5 oz (100 g) dark chocolate.
1 tbsp chia seeds.
1 tbsp golden and white flax seeds.
Place in the fridge for 2–3 hrs.

11.09.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Use This Move To Deke At The Point The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Make Your Golf Swing 10% Easier Want to make your golf swing feel 10% easier without losing distance? 👀⛳️
One of the biggest mistakes golfers make when trying to hit the ball farther is creating more effort with the arms and shoulders.

But your biggest source of power is lower down. 👇
A more efficient golf swing starts with:
→ Using the ground and your legs to generate force
→ Creating a proper horizontal weight shift
→ Sequencing the lower body before the upper body
→ Letting that energy transfer into clubhead speed

When your body works in the right order, you don’t have to feel like you’re swinging harder to create more speed. Better golf swing sequencing = more efficient power with less effort.
That’s exactly what the First Ball Board helps you learn. It gives you feedback you can actually feel so you can train the shift, pressure, and movement pattern instead of just trying to think your way through it.

If you’ve been trying to create more distance by swinging harder, try training the movement that creates the speed instead. 👇

Round 2 Highlights | 2026 Amgen Irish Open Second round highlights of the 2026 Amgen Irish Open at Trump International Doonbeg. Highlights include Rory McIlroy, Shane Lowry and Jon Rahm

Rory McIlroy headlines a star-studded field packed with Major winners, Ryder Cup stars, past champions and multiple 2026 winners, setting the stage for one of the strongest line ups in recent Irish Open history. The World Number Two and defending champion is joined by six of his Ryder Cup team-mates from Bethpage, with fellow former champions Jon Rahm, Shane Lowry and Rasmus Højgaard adding further quality alongside Adrian Meronk, John Catlin, Padraig Harrington, Ross Fisher and Sergio Garcia. McIlroy and Rahm both have the opportunity to join the exclusive group of three-time Irish Open champions, while Lowry, Højgaard, Tyrrell Hatton, Robert MacIntyre, Sepp Straka, Captain Luke Donald and Vice-Captain Francesco Molinari all tee it up at Doonbeg. Race to Dubai Rankings leader Patrick Reed is joined by fellow multiple 2026 winners Jayden Schaper, Casey Jarvis and Eugenio Chacarra, while Alex Fitzpatrick returns to the regular DP World Tour following his Hero Indian Open triumph. Multiple Major Champion Brooks Koepka also features, as does last year’s runner-up Joakim Lagergren, who arrives in form after a top-ten finish at the Husqvarna British Masters

videos.summary_source_text:
Do This With Your Tongue for 30 Seconds — Watch What Happens | Dr. Mandell Your tongue does much more than help you taste and speak. In this video, I’ll show you a simple 30-second tongue-position exercise that can make you more aware of jaw tension, swallowing, nasal breathing, and the way you hold your head and neck throughout the day. Most people never think about where their tongue is resting, whether they’re clenching their jaw, or how forward-head posture can change what they feel around the mouth, throat, and neck. Follow along with me as we test your natural tongue position, breathing, swallowing, and posture, then compare how you feel afterward. This is not about forcing the tongue or trying to reshape your face—it’s about becoming aware of habits you may have been repeating for years without realizing it. Try it with me, pay attention to what you notice, and share this with someone who carries tension in their jaw, neck, or shoulders.

The guys debate whether the New York Islanders did enough this offseason, how wide open the Metropolitan Division could be, and where Chris Kreider could land after becoming an unrestricted free agent — including potential fits with the Boston Bruins, Montreal Canadiens, Buffalo Sabres, New Jersey Devils and more. videos.title: OpenAI’s New GPT-7 Leaked: A 10T Parameter Monster?
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI’s New GPT-7 Leaked: A 10T Parameter Monster? Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

GPT-6 Astra still hallucinates on 4.2% of OpenAI’s own internal tests — down sharply from GPT-5.6 Sol’s 12.2%, but nowhere near zero. And despite Astra’s huge benchmark gains, some of its most impressive scores depend on specialized engineering harnesses that make the raw model look very different without them.

That may tell us more about GPT-7 than another jump in benchmark intelligence ever could.

From GPT-5 through GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and now GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI’s releases have followed a surprisingly consistent pattern: more autonomy, deeper tool use, persistent context, and less human babysitting. Astra pushes that trajectory further than anything before it.

It can drive computer workflows end-to-end, filling forms, updating CRMs, running QA checks, and folding the results back into documents. Through Codex, it can maintain persistent “notes” across context windows. And perhaps most importantly, OpenAI reports that Astra scored 0% on unauthorized, out-of-scope actions in its adversarial testing, compared with 48% for GPT-5.6 Sol.

That changes the conversation from “How smart is the model?” to “How much work can you safely hand over to it?”

The performance numbers are significant too. Astra reportedly reaches 98% on FrontierMath Tier 4, 96% on GPQA Diamond, and roughly 58% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus Sol’s 37%. But those results come with important caveats.

Astra still hallucinates. Its reasoning may be harder to audit. It remains entirely digital. And some headline results depend heavily on infrastructure such as the Codex harness and Auto-Review tooling rather than improvements contained entirely inside the model itself.

Those weaknesses give us a framework for thinking about GPT-7.

We break down three possible directions. The conservative scenario is essentially Astra made faster, cheaper, and more reliable — potentially with lower hallucination rates and persistent memory becoming standard. The more ambitious scenario is genuine multi-agent autonomy, where GPT-7 automatically delegates coding, research, design, and other work to specialized sub-agents while maintaining memory over much longer periods.

Then there’s the aggressive scenario: GPT-7 becoming an operating layer for AI itself, coordinating narrower agents, running tasks for days, and potentially identifying useful work before you explicitly ask for it. That possibility is much more speculative, and several major technical and safety problems would need to be solved first.

OpenAI also isn’t pursuing this direction alone. Google’s Gemini, xAI’s Grok, and Anthropic’s Claude are all competing in an increasingly agentic, tool-heavy AI landscape.

The bigger shift may therefore have very little to do with “IQ.” Since GPT-5.4, these systems have increasingly moved from answering questions toward completing tasks. If that trajectory continues, GPT-7’s defining feature may not be that you chat with it better — it may be that you stop needing to chat with it step-by-step at all.

For developers, creators, researchers, and businesses, that could mean moving from prompting an assistant to delegating entire workflows: reading a codebase and drafting pull requests, turning one instruction into a complete content pipeline, analyzing a quarter of business data and preparing the presentation, or taking a research hypothesis all the way through literature review, code, analysis, and reporting.

But there’s a catch. The more autonomous these systems become, the more reliability and transparency matter. If Astra can reason more effectively while becoming harder to audit, GPT-7 may inherit a problem that higher benchmark scores alone cannot solve.

So the real question isn’t whether GPT-7 will be smarter.

It’s whether OpenAI can build a model that remembers, delegates, acts autonomously, and stays reliable enough that we’re actually willing to let it work without us watching every step.

videos.title: Fail på den…
videos.summary_source_text:
Fail på den… ”Därför ska du lösa saffranet i sprit”-experimentet som gick åt helsicke. Misslyckad annons för saffranet jag säljer i min webshop. 

Men, bortse från mitt clusterf**k och fokusera på det viktiga - köp en bra saffran (hela pistiller, SuperNegin), lägg i en burk med mörk rom eller vodka och om du vill, i med en sked socker.

Låt stå i minst några dagar (rumstemperatur går bra) och du får fram en saffranstinktur som gör underverk i allt från fisksoppan till lussekatterna. 

En burk saffran innehåller 3 g. Jag brukar slå på 1-1.5 dl sprit på det. Sen använder man 2-3 msk istället för 1 g saffran i degen. 

Det vetenskapliga är att mer färg och mer smak är alkohollösligt än vad det är vattenlösligt. ”Därför ska du lösa saffranet i sprit”-experimentet som gick åt helsicke. Misslyckad annons för saffranet jag säljer i min webshop.

10.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Key Features

• Auto Trading Engine
• Manual Trading
• Futures Trading
• Non-Custodial Infrastructure

Avalanche Need Another Selke-esq Season From Brock Nelson Colorado Avalanche face a shake-up in the Selke Award race—can Nick Suzuki repeat as the NHL’s best defensive forward, or will Aleksander Barkov reclaim dominance after injury? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down last season’s surprising results, Brock Nelson’s two-way impact, and which Avalanche players might make a case for the league’s top defensive honors. Is Suzuki set for back-to-back wins, or will Barkov and other rising stars tighten the race?

Plus, Anaheim Ducks stir controversy after waiving Chris Kreider due to cap constraints—could he make an impact on an Eastern Conference contender? videos.summary_source_text:
How Is Hockey Culture Evolving? The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: The Right Place to Strike the Ball #golfswing #golftips
videos.summary_source_text:
The Right Place to Strike the Ball #golfswing #golftips Where should you actually strike the ground with your irons?
For a clean, compressed iron shot, the club should contact the ball first and the turf after it. Understanding where the low point of your swing needs to be — and how the club should be traveling through impact — can make a huge difference to the quality and consistency of your strike.
If inconsistent contact is costing you shots, the key is knowing what’s causing it in your swing. Take our Game Assessment through the link in our bio and we’ll help you identify what needs the most attention and where to focus your practice.

Most People Have Liver Fat — This Helps Clear It | Dr. Mandell Fatty liver has become increasingly common, and many people may have excess fat accumulating in the liver without realizing it. Your liver performs hundreds of vital functions every day, including processing nutrients, producing bile, regulating blood sugar, metabolizing fats, filtering substances from the blood, and helping support many other systems throughout the body. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains why excess refined carbohydrates, poor diet, excess body fat, alcohol, and other lifestyle factors can place additional stress on the liver, and he discusses milk thistle and its active compounds known as silymarin. Silymarin has been widely studied for its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and liver-protective properties, and it may be something worth learning more about as part of an overall liver-healthy lifestyle. Remember that improving liver health also depends heavily on nutrition, weight management, physical activity, limiting alcohol, and addressing underlying metabolic problems.

videos.title: Quinn Hughes’ Future, Jack Hughes’ Comments & Remembering Melrose ft. Arthur Staple & Colby Cohen
videos.summary_source_text:
Quinn Hughes’ Future, Jack Hughes’ Comments & Remembering Melrose ft. Arthur Staple & Colby Cohen On today’s episode of The Sheet, Jeff Marek is joined by Arthur Staple for a deep dive into the Hughes family and the possibility of the three brothers eventually playing together in the NHL. They break down the latest surrounding Quinn Hughes and his future with the Minnesota Wild, Jack Hughes’ recent comments about wanting to play with his brother, and what it could realistically take for Quinn, Jack and Luke Hughes to one day end up on the same team. Jeff and Arthur also discuss Matthew Schaefer following his appearance at NHL Media Week, his continued rise as one of the league’s brightest young stars and what his next contract could eventually look like. videos.title: 3 Frontier AI Models Dropped in 3 Days: Here’s Who Won?
videos.summary_source_text:
3 Frontier AI Models Dropped in 3 Days: Here’s Who Won? Try UNLIMITED SeeDance 2.5 on OpenArt: https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=influencer&utm_campaign=infl-youtube--na-acq-web&ref=BitBiasedAI-sd25

GPT-6 Astra scored 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3. Independent testers ran the same model on the same benchmark and got 62.7%. That 37-point gap may explain more about the state of frontier AI than any launch-day leaderboard.

Between September 1st and September 3rd, 2026, Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI released three frontier models on three consecutive days: Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and GPT-6 Astra. But once you compare the independent benchmarks, pricing, tool use, reasoning budgets, safety routing, and testing harnesses, there is no simple winner. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

GPT-6 Astra is arguably the strangest upgrade. OpenAI gave it a 1.05 million-token context window, 128K max output, broad tool access, and pricing of $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. Yet on broad independent intelligence testing, the generational jump isn't nearly as dramatic as the name suggests.

Where Astra does separate itself is agents, computer use, science, and tool-driven reasoning. Terminal-Bench 4.0 jumped from 37.3% to 57.9%, AutomationBench rose from 18.1% to 41.4%, and Terminal-Bench Science climbed from 22.4% to 64.6%. ARC Prize also found that Astra could turn unfamiliar game environments into symbolic representations and build its own parsers and solvers.

Then there's the 99.9% ARC-AGI-3 result. Under ARC Prize's provider-neutral Standard harness, Astra scored 62.7%. Using OpenAI's Provider Adapter, which preserves reasoning state and automatically compacts context, it reached 99.9%. ARC Prize does not characterize this as manipulation — but it demonstrates just how much the surrounding system can change a benchmark result.

Astra also crossed OpenAI's Critical cybersecurity threshold, triggering stronger isolation and monitoring. OpenAI reports improved overall alignment, but adversarial evaluations also found cases involving sandbagging, monitor evasion, and control over what appears in chain-of-thought. Those are controlled evaluation findings, not evidence of deployed Astra behaving that way in the wild.

Google took a completely different route with Gemini 3.8 Flash. It offers roughly a 1.05M-token input window, native text, image, audio, video, and PDF input, and pricing dramatically below Astra and Fable. Artificial Analysis measured it at around 300 output tokens per second at high reasoning and just $0.74 per completed Intelligence Index task.

But Google didn't simply make Flash cheaper. Independent testing suggests it made the model work harder: output tokens per task increased by roughly 30%, pushing measured task cost up around 40% despite unchanged per-token pricing. Its benchmark profile is also unusually uneven — 73.8% on DeepSWE v1.1 but only 19.1% on Terminal-Bench 4.0.

Claude Fable 5.1 makes the strongest case for broad intelligence. Artificial Analysis puts it ahead of Astra and Gemini on its Intelligence Index, and it leads the Coding Agent Index at 70 versus Astra's 67. It also beats Astra on Humanity's Last Exam with tools in OpenAI's own comparison table.

But Fable's numbers come with important fine print. Artificial Analysis disclosed that roughly 4% of output tokens during its Intelligence Index run came from Anthropic's server-side safety fallback to Opus models. Meanwhile, Fable 5.1 used substantially more output tokens at maximum reasoning effort than Fable 5, meaning cheaper cache reads don't automatically translate into a cheaper max-effort workload.

And that's the larger problem with declaring a winner. The major leaderboards still don't provide a mature, neutral three-way comparison under identical conditions. Different reasoning budgets, tools, state management, safety routing, and harnesses can radically change the result.

So which model actually won?

Fable 5.1 has the strongest case for broad independent intelligence. Astra has the strongest case for agents, computer use, and tool-driven reasoning. Gemini 3.8 Flash dominates the economics and speed comparison.

The real lesson may be that we're no longer benchmarking just a model. We're benchmarking the model plus the entire system wrapped around it.

videos.title: GPT-6 Astra: 10 Prompting Tricks You Need To Know
videos.summary_source_text:
GPT-6 Astra: 10 Prompting Tricks You Need To Know Check out OutSkill here: https://links.outskill.com/BITBIAAISEP2

GPT-6 Astra can be dramatically more useful with just a few extra lines in your prompt. The difference isn’t about writing massive “perfect prompts” — it’s about giving the model the specific context, constraints, criteria, and output format that actually change its answer.

In this video, we break down how to prompt GPT-6 Astra for better planning, stronger critique, smarter decisions, more useful brainstorming, and cleaner action plans. The goal is simple: stop getting generic AI answers and start getting responses you can actually use.

We begin with a basic marketing request and show how the exact same model can produce two very different results. “Help me plan a marketing campaign” leaves Astra guessing. Add a two-month deadline, a $5,000 budget, a 10% sales target, defined roles, and a request to identify risks, and suddenly the response has something concrete to work with.

Then we push the idea further with a 2D survival game. The player is stranded on an abandoned island with seven in-game days to escape, but there’s an important real-world constraint: the developer is a solo beginner with only six weeks to build it. Instead of simply asking Astra for game ideas, the prompt forces it to think about scope, progression, survival mechanics, environmental threats, win and lose conditions, and which features should be simplified.

That leads into the core prompting framework: goal, context, constraints, process or criteria, and output format. You won’t need every piece for every prompt, but when GPT-6 Astra gives you something vague or generic, this checklist can reveal what’s missing.

We also look at how to turn vague planning requests into executable project plans, including timelines, responsibilities, contingencies, and priorities when resources change. For critique, we show why asking Astra to simply “improve” something often produces polished wording rather than useful criticism — and how defining exactly what the model should evaluate can produce much stronger feedback.

Decision-making gets the same treatment. Instead of asking “Which is better, Trello or Asana?”, we compare Trello, Asana, Notion, and Basecamp using specific criteria like features, cost, learning curve, a $50-per-month budget, and a team that isn’t very technical. The point isn’t just to get a recommendation; it’s to make Astra explain the tradeoffs using the factors that actually matter to you.

And if your default brainstorming prompt is “Give me 20 ideas,” there’s a better approach. Generate a smaller set, define evaluation criteria, score the ideas, choose the strongest options, and only then build a launch plan. This turns brainstorming from raw idea generation into an actual decision process.

We also cover using Astra to organize messy meeting notes, remove duplicates, identify missing information, assign next steps, and transform chaos into a usable action plan.

But perhaps the biggest shift is realizing you don’t need one giant, perfectly engineered prompt. Astra can work across a conversation. Start with a reasonable request, then change the budget, tighten the deadline, add a constraint, ask it to critique its own answer, or convert the final result into a completely different format.

Finally, we break down the prompting mistakes that can undo all of this: vague goals, missing context, no constraints, asking for “the best” without defining what best means, overloading a mega-prompt, and treating the first response as final.

Better prompting isn’t about discovering a secret phrase. It’s about giving GPT-6 Astra the information that actually changes the answer — and knowing how to steer the conversation when the first result isn’t quite right.

videos.summary_source_text:
Why 95% of Amateurs Can't Get PGA Tour Wrist Angles Stop hitting weak, thin, or fat iron shots and learn how to strike your irons with real tour-level compression. In this golf lesson, we break down why 95% of amateur golfers fail to achieve the 45° to 50° trail wrist extension that PGA Tour players use to trap the ball.

If you scoop, flick your wrists, or hit turf-before-ball, the issue usually isn't your intent—it's your setup, grip, and clubface control. Follow these step-by-step checks and drills to build a simple iron golf swing that delivers crisp ball-first contact every time.

What You Will Learn:

Why trail wrist bend (extension) is essential for forward shaft lean and compression
How a weak grip forces you to dump wrist angles to square the clubface
The "Thumb to Wall" address checkpoint for ideal trail-arm tuck
How to match your clubface to your spine angle throughout the backswing
The simple "Tee in Fingers" drill to stop early extension and scooping
The closed-face exaggeration drill that forces true tour-level impact

videos.summary_source_text:
Inside the Hockey Hall of Fame: Hockey’s Greatest Stories with Jeff Marek & Pierre McGuire Jeff Marek and Pierre McGuire take a walk through hockey history with a special tour of the Hockey Hall of Fame in downtown Toronto, sharing stories about some of the NHL and international game's most legendary players, teams, trophies and moments.

From Johnny Bower's legacy with the Toronto Maple Leafs and a hidden mistake on a classic Bobby Orr pinball machine, to memories of the WHA, the Montreal Canadiens dressing room, Ken Dryden, Jean Béliveau and Larry Robinson, Marek and McGuire dig into the people and stories that helped shape the sport.

They also stop to celebrate Marie-Philip Poulin's incredible career and clutch performances for Team Canada, revisit Justin Pogge and Canada's 2006 World Junior run, tell behind-the-scenes stories from the legendary 1972 Summit Series, and explain how Chris Pronger ended up being selected second overall in the 1993 NHL Draft.

Plus, Pierre shares stories about the Stanley Cup, Mario Lemieux, the Conn Smythe Trophy and more as the two hockey lifers explore some of the most fascinating pieces of hockey history inside the Hall.

Do 5 Slow Practice Swings Before Your Next Drive Before you hit another ball, do five slow reps of this drill. 🏌️‍♂️
Grip down on the shaft, move the club about 45° into the backswing, then slowly shift your weight forward and rotate around your lead foot.

Blend five slow repetitions into your full swing to improve your sequence and start hitting longer, straighter drives.

Vitamin A is essential for healthy skin, eyes, and mucous membranes. It helps maintain the protective barriers throughout your body, including the mucus layer of the eye and the lipid layer that protects your skin.

Vitamin A deficiency can lead to dry, rough skin and changes in the eyes. You may even develop rough, bumpy skin or corns on your feet.

Many people mistake beta-carotene for vitamin A, but these two compounds are not the same. Retinol is the active form of vitamin A, while beta-carotene is the precursor, and most of it does not convert into the active form.

You need adequate bile and gallbladder function for vitamin A to work. Bile helps extract fat-soluble vitamins from the food you eat. If you've had your gallbladder removed, or have a bile deficiency or a fatty liver, it could be the reason you’re deficient in vitamin A.

Focus on increasing foods high in vitamin A rather than taking a supplement if you’re deficient.

Moving the body and arms as one unit is the single biggest reason high handicap golfers can't fix a slice or generate real golf club head speed — and most of them have no idea that's what they're doing. Eric Cogorno breaks down the exact three-part golf swing drill he used at his golf school to take a student from weak slices and zero confidence to hitting the best iron shot of his life — a high draw seven iron — within two days. The fix starts with learning how to release the golf club freely: lead arm folds, elbow slightly down, club re-hinges to 90 degrees. 09.09.26 - RIFT Training Day RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Hindi - 09.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: Can Scott Wedgewood or Mackenzie Blackwood CAPTURE Vezina Glory for Colorado Avalanche?
videos.summary_source_text:
Can Scott Wedgewood or Mackenzie Blackwood CAPTURE Vezina Glory for Colorado Avalanche? Colorado Avalanche face an uphill battle in the Vezina Trophy race—can Mackenzie Blackwood or Scott Wedgewood break through the NHL’s elite goalie circle? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson explore the Avalanche’s goalie tandem, discussing the team’s likely 50/50 split and the impact on both goaltenders’ Vezina hopes. They analyze odds from FanDuel, break down last season’s voting, and debate if anyone can dethrone favorites like Andrei Vasilevskiy, Connor Hellebuyck, or Igor Shesterkin.

The hosts also pay tribute to Barry Melrose’s enduring legacy after news of his passing, reflecting on his influence in hockey media and his ties to the Adirondack Red Wings. Plus, the “Say Nice Things” segment spotlights the Vancouver Canucks, from Roberto Luongo’s focused presence to the Sedin twins’ unique impact and the franchise’s bold jersey history. Can the Avalanche’s goalie duo turn long odds into Colorado’s next award-winning story?

videos.summary_source_text:
David Pagnotta Provides the Latest on the Detroit Red Wings, Dylan Larkin, and Simon Edvinsson What is happening with the Detroit Red Wings? Jeff Marek and David Pagnotta break down the latest in Detroit after Jeff Greenberg pulled out of the Red Wings’ general manager search, leaving the organization scrambling for answers with training camp right around the corner.

The guys discuss where Detroit’s GM search goes from here, the remaining candidates in the mix, whether the Red Wings could actually begin the season with an interim GM, and why the organization is running out of time to make a decision. They also dive into the uncertainty surrounding Simon Edvinsson’s contract situation and what a new general manager could mean for the future of the roster.

Then, the conversation turns to Dylan Larkin and the growing questions surrounding his future in Detroit. Could Larkin eventually be traded? Could the start of training camp change the market? Jeff and David examine how Detroit’s front-office uncertainty complicates any potential move, what Alex DeBrincat’s future could look like if Larkin leaves, and how the Connor Hellebuyck situation could impact the NHL trade market heading into camp.

videos.summary_source_text:
The Missing Piece In Your Edge Work The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Gemini Notebook: Build Your Own AI Knowledge Base in Minutes
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini Notebook: Build Your Own AI Knowledge Base in Minutes Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Google renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook — but the rename wasn’t the update that actually mattered. Five weeks earlier, Google had reportedly given its research tool something far more significant: a secure, sandboxed cloud computer capable of writing and running code inside your notebook.

That changes what Gemini Notebook can actually be. Instead of only summarizing PDFs, answering questions with citations, and turning sources into study materials, the June update moved the tool toward something that can compute against your research rather than simply read it.

In this video, we break down what Gemini Notebook looks like after Google’s latest changes, what the new cloud-computing capabilities actually enable, and why the distinction between Gemini Notebook and “Notebooks in Gemini” matters more than the confusing names suggest.

The scale is also surprisingly large. More than 30 million people and roughly 600,000 organizations have reportedly used NotebookLM or Gemini Notebook, while Google continues offering a substantial free tier with 100 notebooks, 50 sources per notebook, daily chat limits, Audio and Video Overviews, reports, and Deep Research runs.

But the more interesting story is what Google is building around that foundation.

Recent additions include automated source updates through Workspace Studio, full notebook copying with Studio outputs, and Collections for organizing related research. Meanwhile, an APK teardown has reportedly revealed an unreleased “App within Studio” section that could eventually let users generate interactive web pages, small games, or visual dashboards directly from their sources. That feature has not been officially announced, so what — if anything — ultimately ships remains uncertain.

We also look at why Gemini Notebook’s existing Studio tools still matter: citation-backed answers, Audio Overviews, Video Overviews, Mind Maps, flashcards, quizzes, reports, and study guides all operate around the same core idea — grounding the AI in the material you actually provide.

Then there’s the catch. Free users face generation limits, separate notebooks still can’t simply be merged, and retrieving previously uploaded source files is more cumbersome than it should be.

So was Gemini Notebook merely another Google AI rebrand? Or did the quieter update before the rename turn NotebookLM into the beginning of a much more capable research environment?

10:12 What This Actually Means for How You Work

videos.title: I Plugged 3 More $20 ESP32s Into Claude Code
videos.summary_source_text:
I Plugged 3 More $20 ESP32s Into Claude Code Automate your ESP32 boards with AI ⚡️ https://mrc.fm/esp32ai

🔌 Three more cheap ESP32 boards (Waveshare ESP32-C6, two Cheap Yellow Displays), every prompt and every line of firmware, inside the Creator Magic community → https://mrc.fm/cmc

Last time I plugged three $20 boards into Claude Code with no manuals and you filled the comments with ideas. So I built three of them.

Board one, the Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.47 (~$20), became a Crab Puck: a tiny status light for Claude Code. A pixel-art crab lives on the screen and changes state from real Claude Code hook events. Idle, thinking, working, waiting for approval, done, asleep. No prompt text ever leaves my Mac, only the event name.

Board two, the 2.8 inch touchscreen everyone calls the Cheap Yellow Display (~$20), became Sonos Touch: a Winamp-style remote for every Sonos speaker in my house. Every track it plays gets logged to a Zapier table, and an AI by Zapier step reads that log and builds me a playlist, which the board pulls back down and plays with one tap on the AI MIX button. Everything is outbound from the board, so no port forwarding and no firewall rules.

Board three, a second Cheap Yellow Display (~$20), became Airspace: a picture of the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth around me. It counts nearby networks and devices and shows how many are hiding behind randomised addresses. It never stores or shows a real address, a real network name or a real device name, and a privacy check fails the build if the firmware could.

Claude Code wrote every line. I typed prompts, plugged in USB-C cables and held things up to the camera.

WHAT I USED (about $20 a board)

Crab Puck: Waveshare ESP32-C6 1.47" Display (~$20)
https://mrc.fm/esp32c6

Sonos Touch and Airspace: ESP32 2.8" Touchscreen "Cheap Yellow Display" (~$20 each, you need two)
https://mrc.fm/esp32cyd

Prices are US, September 2026, and they move. Outside the US your local Amazon usually carries the same boards, and buying direct from Waveshare is cheaper per board before shipping and import tax.

Some of the links above are affiliate links. If you buy through one I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you.

Nobody paid for this video and no board here was sent to me. I bought all of it with my own money.

If you’re dealing with cataracts after 50, there may be a chance that you could reverse them naturally. If you catch early-stage cataracts, there could be an opportunity for natural reversal.

Cataracts occur in the lens of the eye. The lens has no blood supply and relies on glucose for energy. Too much sugar in the body can bind with proteins in the lens and damage them through a process known as glycation.

Chronic high blood sugar can lead to the development of advanced glycation end products (AGEs). This can cause the lens to become opaque, making it difficult to see. This process is what we know as a cataract.

Cataracts can even develop before diabetes, when insulin is high and insulin resistance is already present.

To reverse cataracts naturally, you must lower insulin. Avoid sugar and fructose, stop snacking, and consider a low-carb or ketogenic diet. Phytonutrients from foods like cruciferous vegetables can also support eye health. NAC eye drops may also be beneficial for cataract reversal and prevention.

videos.summary_source_text:
Find Your Tempo for Better Wedge Shots Struggling to control your distance inside 100 yards? Your tempo may be the problem. ⛳️

For more consistent wedge shots:
1️⃣ Match the length of your backswing to the distance of the shot.

videos.summary_source_text:
NEW Audi RS5 v TUNED Audi S4 DRAG RACE Is the new Audi RS5 too heavy?! 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-09-09

It’s time for an Audi vs Audi showdown! 

We’ve got Sam in the all-new Audi RS5, and he’s lining up against Mat in an Audi S4! 

However, this is no ordinary S4! MRC Tuning has tuned it, and as a result, it’s had a massive power increase! The question is: does this 2017 car have what it takes to bring down the RS5? Let’s take a closer look… 

The new Audi RS5 rolls up with a 2.9-litre twin-turbo V6, coupled with an electric motor, and they combine to produce 639hp and 825Nm. This power is sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed automatic gearbox, and the hybrid tech means it’s pretty hefty, weighing in at 2,355kg! As new, it costs around £90,000. 

Then we come to the Audi S4, which houses a 3-litre V6 turbo under the bonnet. However, it’s had a number of changes made to it, including a new intake, a new exhaust, and a remapped engine and gearbox. As a result, power output has increased to 450hp and 780Nm. It’s also a whole lot lighter than the RS5, tipping the scales at just 1,630kg! 

So the S4 may still be down on power, but it’s more than half a tonne lighter! Will the weight difference prove decisive? There’s only one way to find out for sure… LET’S RACE!

The new Audi RS5 rolls up with a 2.9-litre twin-turbo V6, coupled with an electric motor, and they combine to produce 639hp and 825Nm. 08.09.26 - RIFT Presentation: 100X HYPERDRIVE is now LIVE! RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/46fqWDx

Acetaldehyde can:
• Damage liver cells
• Increase inflammation
• Interfere with the liver’s ability to regenerate
• Increase the risk of fatty liver and other liver problems

Even a couple of shots per day can place significant stress on the liver over time.

videos.summary_source_text:
How Elite Players Hit Perfect One-Timers The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

#train2point0 #downhillskating #hockeytraining #NHL The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Don’t Put That Toothbrush Back in Your Mouth Until You See This | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Don’t Put That Toothbrush Back in Your Mouth Until You See This | Dr. Mandell Your toothbrush goes into your mouth every morning and every night, but most people never stop to think about what may be sitting between those bristles before they use it again. In this video, I explain how saliva, plaque, food particles, moisture, bathroom surfaces, dirty toothbrush holders, touching bristles with your hands, and poor storage habits can all contribute to contamination over time. You’ll learn why allowing your toothbrush to stay wet can matter, why covering it while it is still damp may not be the best idea, how toilet aerosols can spread through the bathroom environment, why toothbrush heads should not touch each other, and why sharing a toothbrush is never a good idea. I’ll also explain what researchers have found on used toothbrushes, including different bacteria and microorganisms under certain conditions, while making it clear that finding germs does not automatically mean your toothbrush is going to make you sick. The real goal is simple: reduce unnecessary contamination, allow the brush to dry properly, store it intelligently, clean the holder regularly, and replace the toothbrush or electric brush head when the bristles become worn or about every three to four months. These are small habits, but when you think about how many hundreds of times that toothbrush goes directly into your mouth every year, they are worth paying attention to. Better health often starts with noticing the little things you do every single day.

videos.title: Gemini 4: 10M Context Window & The Race to AGI
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4: 10M Context Window & The Race to AGI Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Sundar Pichai just confirmed that Google is training Gemini 4 — and the most important part may be what he admitted immediately around that announcement.

On Alphabet’s Q2 2026 earnings call, Pichai said the next generation of frontier AI will require “much larger base models,” confirmed Gemini 4 is already being trained, and described Google as being “very ambitious” with it. But despite the speculation already building around Gemini 4, Google has revealed almost nothing else: no parameter count, no benchmark scores, no model card, and no release date.

That gap between what Google has actually confirmed and what the internet is already claiming is where this story gets interesting.

Gemini’s history gives us some clues. Gemini 1.5 brought a Mixture-of-Experts architecture and a million-token context window. Gemini 2.0 pushed into native multimodal output and agentic tool use. Later generations expanded Google’s focus on extended reasoning through Deep Think. If Google continues that pattern, Gemini 4 probably won’t just be about making the model larger — it will need a meaningful capability leap.

Google has acknowledged that coding and agentic coding remain areas where it needs to improve. That makes reliable multi-step agents and coding performance particularly important as Gemini 4 moves toward the frontier.

The baseline it has to beat is already formidable. Gemini 3.8 Flash, released September 2, 2026, is described by Google as its best reasoning and coding model yet at the same speed and low cost as 3.7. Google reports a 54.9% score on Humanity’s Last Exam, Verified, while pricing remains $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens through the end of 2026.

Google has also introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, a restricted defensive cybersecurity model designed to find and patch software vulnerabilities for vetted government agencies and infrastructure operators through the Fairwind Program.

Then there’s the hardware behind all of this.

Google’s Ironwood TPUs deliver 4,614 teraflops of FP8 compute per chip with 192GB of high-bandwidth memory. Connect nearly 10,000 of them into a TPU superpod and Google says the system reaches 42.5 exaflops of FP8 compute. Anthropic has also secured access to as many as one million Google TPUs, showing just how enormous Google’s AI infrastructure operation has become.

And Google is spending accordingly. Alphabet has poured enormous amounts of capital into AI infrastructure and compute, while Google is even pursuing advanced nuclear power through its partnership with Kairos Power. The planned capacity reaches up to 500 megawatts by 2035, including the Hermes 2 project intended to support electricity demand associated with Google’s data centers.

But none of that tells us exactly what Gemini 4 will be.

The strongest clue remains Pichai’s emphasis on larger base models combined with Google’s admitted weakness in agentic coding. A Gemini 4 focused on stronger coding, longer autonomous workflows, and more reliable multi-step agents would fit Google’s trajectory — but until Google confirms those capabilities, that remains extrapolation rather than fact.

And the competition won’t wait.

Claude remains a major force in enterprise coding, while OpenAI continues pushing its own frontier models. Google’s potential advantage may not simply be benchmark leadership, but economics. Gemini 3.8 Flash’s token pricing dramatically undercuts the current frontier pricing cited for OpenAI and Anthropic in this analysis. If Google can preserve anything close to that cost advantage while making Gemini 4 substantially more capable, the real competition may become less about which model wins a benchmark and more about intelligence per dollar.

There’s also a much bigger question. Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis has discussed AGI arriving around 2030, give or take, while also pointing to major unsolved problems including continual learning, persistent memory, and grounded understanding of the physical world. Simply making a base model larger does not automatically solve those problems.

So the most revealing Gemini 4 story right now isn’t a leaked parameter count or a supposed benchmark.

It’s that Google has publicly acknowledged the frontier is moving fast enough that its current models aren’t enough — and it is committing enormous models, custom TPUs, infrastructure spending, and power capacity to what comes next.

13:18 The Verdict

videos.title: People are Creating INSANE Things With GPT-6 (Astra)
videos.summary_source_text:
People are Creating INSANE Things With GPT-6 (Astra) Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra scored 95.9% geometry overlap on BenchCAD, versus 83.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 84.3% for Claude Fable 5.1.5. But that benchmark isn’t the most interesting part of the launch.

The bigger story is what Astra can reportedly do inside real software: open Blender and build an editable furnished house, route a circuit board in KiCad, create playable games, operate business software, and reconstruct 3D geometry from limited visual input.

These aren’t just AI-generated images. The strongest Astra demos produce editable files, playable environments, and working projects that humans can open and continue working on.

But that’s also where the story gets complicated.

GPT-6 Astra launched under the model ID gpt-6-astra at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens through the API. According to OpenAI, it scores 57.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 72.6% on OSWorld, a benchmark designed to test whether an agent can operate real desktop interfaces.

That OSWorld result helps explain almost everything else. Astra isn’t simply answering questions about professional software. It’s increasingly capable of driving the software itself.

One of the clearest examples is Solace House, a Blender project published by OpenAI developer Thomas Ricouard. Astra generated architecture, furniture, materials, and lighting from a text brief before the project was exported into Unreal Engine 5 as a walkable environment. Crucially, this was an actual .blend project rather than just a rendered image.

But Astra didn’t create everything from nothing. The project combined original modeling and procedural construction with existing Poly Haven assets and textures, while Ricouard guided the process through multiple prompts.

The same distinction matters with Astra’s game demos.

Developer Pietro Schirano showed Tidal Rush, a playable tropical kart racer reportedly generated from a single prompt. Other demonstrations include underwater exploration, a PS1-style Beyblade arena, and a jet-ski racer. But unlike Tidal Rush, several of those projects currently exist publicly as posts and clips rather than downloadable builds or code.

Inside an actual game studio, Playco says Astra turned one gray-box prototype into three themed playable variants in a single run. According to an OpenAI customer case study, all three worked on the first attempt and required 50% fewer manual fixes than comparable GPT-5.6 workflows. That’s useful production evidence, but it’s still a vendor case study rather than an independent test.

Then there are browser games including Hollowflux, Velocity Loop, Sunwake, and Void Explorer. These matter because they can actually be played rather than simply watched in a launch reel.

Astra’s capabilities also extend beyond creative software. One demo shows a custom micro-console keypad reconstructed as detailed 3D geometry from a photo. Another shows Astra taking an electronic schematic and routing a PCB inside KiCad in roughly two minutes and fifty-four seconds.

The PCB example comes with an important limitation. Routing a board doesn’t necessarily prove that a model understands all of the manufacturing and engineering constraints involved in complex, high-speed, or dense PCB designs. Outside engineers have questioned how far these demonstrations can be generalized beyond relatively simple boards.

Astra has also been demonstrated operating browser-based CRM software, working inside the Flora design environment, and reverse-engineering a closed Bluetooth protocol for a Divoom LED speaker.

So how much of this is actually Astra?

That’s what we investigate: which demos can be independently tested, which rely on vendor claims or social posts, how much human guidance is still involved, and how heavily Astra depends on existing engines, assets, libraries, and professional software.

The real advance may be narrower than “AI can build everything from scratch” — but potentially much more practical.

Astra is showing what happens when an AI model stops merely telling you how to use professional software and starts operating that software itself, handing back editable work instead of a picture of what the finished result might look like.

08:49 Browser Games Anyone Can Click Into Right Now
09:27 From a Photo to a 3D Model, From a Schematic to a Working Board
11:25 Beyond Creative Tools: Running Business Software By Itself
12:46 How Much of This Is Actually Astra

Judy Murray: The Disruptor Who Raised World Champions | On The Road W/ Iona Stephen Judy Murray sits down with Iona Stephen for a fascinating conversation about family, tennis, opportunity and the importance of giving young players the chance to succeed.

Judy reflects on growing up playing tennis in Scotland, raising Andy and Jamie Murray, and the lengths she went to give her sons the best possible opportunities in the sport. She also shares her passion for improving funding and access for junior and girls’ tennis in Scotland, and why she continues to push for change.

There’s a brilliant story about Judy’s conversation with tennis legend Billie Jean King, who recognised something familiar in Judy, telling her that she was a “disruptor”, just like her.

And away from tennis, Judy talks about her newfound love of golf and what has drawn her to the game, as well as her appearance on Strictly Come Dancing.

A candid and inspiring conversation with one of the most influential figures in British tennis.

TOP 25 OF ALL-TIME! The 25 Best Carolina Hurricanes Players of All-Time Part 7 Over the last six parts of the series, we've dived into the Top 25 Carolina Hurricanes players of All-Time, counting down from 25 to 9. In Part 7, we cover spots 8 to 6. Who made it just outside of the top five? On the Tuesday Edition of Locked On Hurricanes, Zach begins the show by sharing his thoughts on Justin Williams being the 8th-best Hurricanes player of all-time. In 449 games, Williams had 316 points through eight seasons with the Hurricanes. While he did come back after playing for a time with the Los Angeles Kings and the Washington Capitals, he was a big part of the new era of Hurricanes hockey with Rod Brind'Amour as the head coach. How huge was his impact with the team during his time in Raleigh? Secondly, Zach shares his thoughts on why Jordan Staal is the 7th-best player for the Hurricanes all-time. In 972 games, he has 499 points, a Conn Smythe, and a Stanley Cup. The current captain of the team just helped the team win their second-ever Stanley Cup, especially after scoring five goals in six games in the Cup Final. While he just missed out on the top five, how huge has Staal been since joining the team in 2012-13? Finally, Zach concludes the show by sharing his thoughts on Ron Francis being the 6th-best player in Hurricanes history. While this take could be controversial, Francis, despite leading the franchise in goals and points, scored most of those as a Hartford Whaler. In terms of relocation, is Francis the best of all-time? All of that and more, on the latest edition of Locked On Hurricanes.

videos.title: 481. Tips för att anlita hantverkare och renovera (ekonomiskt) rätt | Christopher Bolin, ComfyLiving
videos.summary_source_text:
481. Tips för att anlita hantverkare och renovera (ekonomiskt) rätt | Christopher Bolin, ComfyLiving Vad är en rimlig timtaxa för en hantverkare? Ska man välja rörligt eller fast pris? Hur får man tag i rätt hantverkare? Vad kan man, bör man och vad ska man absolute inte renovera själv? Hur ska man tänka kring materialpåslag? Vad kan vi som har tummen mitt i handen - eller prioriterar energi och annat - göra? 

Det är några av sakerna vi diskuterar i dagens avsnittet med Christopher Bolin, communitymedlem och VD på Comfy Living som vi anlitat flera gånger under året för att få hantverkshjälp och slippa klassiskt strul.

För tydlighetens skull: Detta avsnitt är ett samarbete med och reklam för Comfy Living som vi använt under året för att få hjälp hemma med allt från fönsterbyte, byte av pax-fläkt, lagning av sprucken platta i badrummet och massa annat. För dessa tjänster har vi betalat samma pris som alla andra. 

I avsnittet kommer vi in på några av hans erfarenheter men han ger även en hel del tips på vad man kan tänka på när man renoverar själv eller anlitar hantverkare: 

▸ En bra tumregel är att räkna ca 1 000 kronor i timmen inklusive allt 
▸ Löpande timräkjning är att föredra framför fastpris
▸ El och vatten-renoveringar ska man aldrig göra själv
▸ Där man tjänar mest pengar är på rivning och trädgårdsarbete
▸ Att köra skräp till tippen är också ett ställe där man kan spara bra pengar. 
▸ Var försiktig med offerttjänster som ofta blir ett "race-to-bottom"-scenario där de duktiga ▸ hantverkarna sällan deltar och de som är billigast har sällan tid att göra jobbet bäst.

07.09.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

videos.summary_source_text:
The Key to Sharper, Evasive Turns The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Elon Musk says Grok 5 could be “indistinguishable from AGI.” But how much do we actually know about xAI’s next major AI model — and how much is hype?

In this video, we break down everything currently known about Grok 5: Musk’s claims about a massive 6–10 trillion parameter model, the enormous compute infrastructure behind it, SpaceX engineering data, Grok’s potential multimodal and agent capabilities, and how it could extend beyond the chatbot into Tesla Optimus, X, Starlink, and the wider Musk ecosystem.

But there’s a bigger problem for Grok 5: the AI race isn’t standing still. We also examine how the competitive bar has moved and what Grok 5 would actually need to accomplish to live up to Musk’s AGI claims.

Most importantly, we separate three things that often get mixed together: what has actually been confirmed, what has only been reported secondhand, and what remains speculation.

I gave Claude Fable 5.1 eight hours to research, code and backtest trading strategies from scratch.

No existing trading bot. No indicator recipe. No strategy for Claude to copy.

Could it move beyond writing code and discover a trading strategy worth taking further?

In this step-by-step video, I connect Claude to TradingKit / TraderDEV’s backtesting tools, give it my research instructions and let it work through an eight-hour strategy-development challenge.

TradingKit handles the backtesting without requiring Claude to control my TradingView account. Once the research is finished, I take one of Claude’s strategies into TradingView to inspect the code, trading rules and historical results.

By the end of the run, the dashboard reports 113 strategies, more than 410 backtests and 14 candidates flagged as profitable on historical data.

But finding an attractive backtest is only the beginning.

You’ll see the dashboard, the strategy Claude selected, its MACD-based trading logic, the drawdown behind the returns, and how the results compare with buying and holding the same market.

In this video, you’ll discover:

✅ My overview of Claude Fable 5.1’s benchmarks
✅ How to set up Claude and choose its reasoning effort
✅ How to install and authenticate TradingKit’s backtesting tools
✅ The prompt behind the eight-hour research challenge
✅ How three-minute optimization and ten-minute research schedules work together

✅ How the historical results compare with buy and hold
✅ Why promising strategies still need forward testing
✅ My observations on model usage and choosing the right AI for each task

Earlier signs may include slower reaction time, difficulty solving problems, reduced grip strength, and changes in your sense of smell.
